I work in the academic office and we want to review the grade distributions for our Spring 2014 courses and also collect student feedback through a survey.

First, please look up all courses from Spring 2014 in our learning management system. For each course, I need to analyze the assignment submissions to compute grade statistics: the average score, the median score, the pass rate (percentage of submissions with score >= 60), and the total number of distinct students who submitted graded work (count each student once).

Create an Excel file called "Grade_Distribution_Report.xlsx" in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet called "Course Grades" should have columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Avg_Grade, Median_Grade, Pass_Rate, and Total_Students. Include one row per Spring 2014 course. The second sheet called "Summary" should have columns Metric and Value with rows for Total_Courses (number of Spring 2014 courses), Overall_Avg_Grade (average across all courses), Highest_Avg_Course (name of course with highest average grade), and Lowest_Avg_Course (name of course with lowest average grade). Write all computed numbers as plain numeric values (do not write Excel formulas), and use the course code and full course name as they appear in the learning management system.

Second, create a survey form titled "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey" to collect student opinions. The form should have at least 4 questions: overall satisfaction with the course (as a choice question with options Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor), teaching quality rating (as a choice question with options 1 through 5), how they found the workload (as a choice question with options Too Light, Manageable, Heavy, Overwhelming), and an open-ended suggestions question (as a text question, not required).

Finally, send an email from registrar@university.edu to students@university.edu with the subject "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey" informing students about the survey and encouraging them to participate.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep the large submission reads outside the main context with exactly one parallel collector wave, and let the main agent itself produce the workbook, the form and the email — no second wave.

The main agent resolves the accessible task workspace, calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, and retains exactly the six Spring 2014 courses by full name/code (expected course_ids 6, 8, 12, 15, 19, 22). Validate unique course IDs, then dispatch one explore collector per course.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 6 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per literal Spring course. Every collector follows the same literal recipe with only its course substituted:

1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Collector for course_id=6 (course_code and course_name as listed). A strictly read-only Canvas collector: call canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=6, per_page=100, page=1), then keep calling page=2,3,... while pagination.has_more is true. The tool result may be truncated in the chat preview — always read the FULL JSON from the output_path file given in the result. A submission counts as graded iff it has a non-null numeric score field and workflow_state == "graded". Scores are on a 0-100 percentage scale. Aggregate all graded submissions in one script execution and return ONLY the compact JSON {course_id:6, course_code, course_name, avg_score, median_score, pass_rate, total_students, graded_count, pages}, where avg_score/median_score are the mean/median of graded scores, pass_rate = 100 * count(score >= 60) / graded_count, and total_students = number of DISTINCT user_ids among graded submissions. Do not return the row set, write any workspace file, or modify Canvas.
2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Collector for course_id=8 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Collector for course_id=12 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
4. explore 3 (enterprise-data-analyst 3): Collector for course_id=15 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
5. explore 4 (enterprise-data-analyst 4): Collector for course_id=19 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
6. explore 5 (enterprise-data-analyst 5): Collector for course_id=22 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.

After Wave 1, verify all six handoffs in one single pass (never per-course iteration): exactly one handoff per course, non-null statistics, graded_count > 0. Compute the four Summary metrics from the six unrounded course averages: Overall_Avg_Grade as the equal-weight arithmetic mean of the six course averages (not a submission-weighted global average); Highest_Avg_Course / Lowest_Avg_Course by unrounded course averages with course_code ascending only as a tie-break; Total_Courses = 6.

The main agent then completes every output directly, with no further delegation: (a) build Grade_Distribution_Report.xlsx in the resolved workspace with exactly two sheets — "Course Grades" with header Course_Code, Course_Name, Avg_Grade, Median_Grade, Pass_Rate, Total_Students and one row per course, and "Summary" with header Metric, Value and the four metric rows — all values plain numbers (no Excel formulas), then read both populated ranges back; (b) call create_form(title="Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey") exactly once, add the four required questions sequentially with exact types/options/required flags (satisfaction choice Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor; teaching-quality choice 1-5; workload choice Too Light/Manageable/Heavy/Overwhelming; open-ended optional text suggestions), and verify with get_form(formId); (c) search Sent mail for From registrar@university.edu, To students@university.edu, subject Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey, send exactly once only if no exact match exists, and read the retained message back. Finally run ONE reconciliation turn covering the workbook read-back, the form ID and the sent message, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any agent after Wave 1, do not add a verification wave, and do not expose raw submission rows to the main context.

nodes.text:
Task: Compute grade distribution statistics from the Canvas LMS for all Spring 2014 courses at Open University.

Background: I work in the academic office and need per-course grade statistics computed from assignment submissions. The following 6 courses are the confirmed Spring 2014 courses (course ID, course code, full name as it appears in Canvas):
- Course ID 6: BBB-2014B — "Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014)"
- Course ID 8: CCC-2014B — "Creative Computing & Culture (Spring 2014)"
- Course ID 12: DDD-2014B — "Data-Driven Design (Spring 2014)"
- Course ID 15: EEE-2014B — "Environmental Economics & Ethics (Spring 2014)"
- Course ID 19: FFF-2014B — "Foundations of Finance (Spring 2014)"
- Course ID 22: GGG-2014B — "Global Governance & Geopolitics (Spring 2014)"

For EACH course compute these 4 statistics from the assignment submissions:
1. Avg_Grade: mean score across ALL graded assignment submissions in the course.
2. Median_Grade: median score across ALL graded assignment submissions.
3. Pass_Rate: percentage of graded submissions with score >= 60, i.e. (count of scores >= 60) / (total count of scores) * 100.
4. Total_Students: number of DISTINCT students (user_id) who have at least one graded submission (count each student once).

Method:
- For each course, list all assignments with mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignments.
- For each assignment, fetch ALL submissions. You may use mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignment_submissions per assignment, or the bulk mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions endpoint. IMPORTANT: page through EVERY page (per_page=100, follow pagination.has_more until false) — do not skip or truncate pages, the courses have ~1000-2500 submissions per assignment.
- Include ONLY submissions with workflow_state == "graded" AND a non-null "score" value. Include late and on-time submissions alike. Ignore ungraded/missing submissions.
- The "score" field is a numeric percentage on a 0-100 scale (already verified: a 1-point CMA quiz has scores like 100.00/80.00; an 18-point TMA has scores like 67.00/70.00). Use the score values as-is — do NOT divide by points_possible.
- Assignments with zero submissions simply contribute nothing to the stats.
- Use Python (mcp__local__python_execute is NOT available to you — you have only Canvas read tools, so compute manually or report raw counts; if you can run read-only computations do so, otherwise compute the aggregates carefully from the collected data and show your work).

Deliverable (your final report): One row per course with: course_id, course_code, full course name as in Canvas, Avg_Grade (2 decimals), Median_Grade (2 decimals), Pass_Rate (as a number, e.g. 72.5 meaning 72.5%), Total_Students (integer). Also report the min and max score observed per course (to confirm the 0-100 scale), the total number of assignments considered per course, and flag any anomalies (e.g., assignments with zero submissions, missing data). Be exact — do not approximate counts.
Compute Spring 2014 grade stats

Task: Create a Google Form for a student feedback survey and send an announcement email. You are acting on behalf of the Open University academic office.

Step 1 — Create the Google Form:
- Use mcp__google_forms__create_form with:
  - title: "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey"
  - description: "Please share your feedback on your Spring 2014 courses. Your responses help us improve teaching and course design."
- Then add these 4 questions IN THIS ORDER:
  1. mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question: questionTitle "Overall satisfaction with the course", options ["Excellent", "Good", "Fair", "Poor"], required = true.
  2. mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question: questionTitle "Teaching quality rating", options ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"], required = true.
  3. mcp__google_forms__add_multiple_choice_question: questionTitle "How did you find the workload?", options ["Too Light", "Manageable", "Heavy", "Overwhelming"], required = true.
  4. mcp__google_forms__add_text_question: questionTitle "Any suggestions for improvement?", required = false (open-ended, not required).

Step 2 — Send the announcement email:
- Use mcp__emails__send_email with:
  - from_addr: "registrar@university.edu"
  - to: "students@university.edu"
  - subject: "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey"
  - body (plain text): A short, encouraging message informing students about the Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey and asking them to participate (e.g., their feedback is valuable and will help improve courses). If the Google Form URL/link is available from Step 1, include it in the body; otherwise state that the survey is available via their course pages.

Deliverable (your final report): Report the created form's ID and title, the list of questions added (with types/options) to confirm all 4 are present, and confirmation that the email was sent (recipient, subject, message ID if returned), plus the form URL if available.
Create survey form and send email

You are a data-collection agent for the Open University academic office. Your ONLY job is to fetch EVERY page of assignment submissions for ONE Canvas course so the data can be analyzed offline later. Do NOT compute any statistics, do NOT analyze the content — just fetch pages.

Your course ID: 6

Steps:
1. Call mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions with course_id=6, per_page=100, page=1.
2. Important: When a page output is larger than 50,000 characters, the harness truncates what you see and automatically saves the FULL output to a file under the workspace's .tool_results directory (the response tells you the output_path). That is expected — you do NOT need to read the full file.
3. Keep calling with page=2, 3, 4, ... incrementing by 1. STOP ONLY when you receive a page whose "submissions" array is empty (i.e., the response/preview shows "submissions": [] — that means the end of the data). For any non-empty page the preview will begin with "submissions": [ { ... entries. Do not stop early — a full page of 100 submissions is non-empty, so keep going until you hit the empty page.
4. Do not worry about pagination fields if you cannot see them in a truncated preview; the empty-submissions page is your reliable stop signal.

Deliverable (your final report): state the course_id, the total number of pages you fetched (including the final empty page), and confirmation that the last page had an empty submissions array (i.e., you reached the end of the data).
Fetch all submission pages per course
